text:
ashley: ran a focused nsys on a repro harness hitting the 1024-seqlen path. seeing periodic cudaMalloc spikes (10-30ms) aligned with batcher flushes. putting traces here: https://perf.redwood/2034567890/trace.nsys :thinking_face:

vikram: can you paste the nsys kernel timeline snippet? my hunch is a kernel selector fallback that triggers host allocs when a fused kernel isn't picked.

ashley: snippet below (trimmed):
```
[GPU0] time(ms)  kernel                        mem   notes
  1123.2     aten::fused_attention_forward    ---  small-kernel (fast)
  1123.5     cudaMalloc                       18ms allocation spike
  1123.6     aten::attention_dispatch         ---  fallback to generic
  1123.9     kernel: generic_attention        ---  higher latency
```

marco: interesting. perfetto heap snapshot shows a ladder of many ~32KB slab objects not being reused. looks like kvcache arena handing out small chunks instead of recycling. might be fragmentation + small-alloc churn.

sophia: steps to validate: 1) reproduce with allocator logging on (RD_ALLOC=debug) 2) run with arena->min_slab doubled 3) force kernel-selector to prefer fused for seq>=512. results should isolate whether alloc churn causes kernel fallbacks or the other way around.

perf-bot: automated diff summary for nsys run vs baseline:
  - p50 token latency +11%
  - observed 7 cudaMalloc events per 1000 requests (baseline 0.6)
  - KV cache hit ratio unchanged
  - small-kernel execution count increased during spikes

vikram: that diff suggests allocator activity is correlated but not necessarily causal. we need stack traces for the cudaMallocs. ashley, can you capture `LD_PRELOAD=libcuda_mallochook.so` style stackshots or use cudaMallocAsync trace?

ashley: capturing now. attaching a short stack dump:
```
#0  libcudart.so cudaMalloc
#1  runtime::Arena::alloc_chunk
#2  runtime::KVCache::ensure_slot
#3  runtime::Batcher::flush
#4  runtime::Dispatch::route_request
```

marco: that points at KV cache fragmentation forcing new allocations on flush. when batcher flushes it asks for fresh KV slots, arena falls back to cudaMalloc when its free-lists are empty.

sophia: actionable tuning:
  - pre-warm arena on startup with `--arena-warmup=128`
  - increase slab_size from 64KB to 256KB for model with long context
  - enable aggressive reuse: `--arena-reuse-threshold=0.8`
  - batcher change: avoid simultaneous flush of >8 streams for seq>512 (stagger flush)

vikram: also evaluate kernel selector policy: it currently picks fused only if KV slot allocation completes within 2ms. if allocator spikes >2ms we wrongly route to generic kernel. maybe change to optimistic path: pick fused and fall back if allocation fails.

ashley: tried `--arena-warmup=128` + larger slab in a quick loop: cudaMalloc spikes drop to ~1 per 10k requests, p95 token latency down 6%. will run longer A/B overnight.

marco: can you also save perfetto heap diff and nvtx ranges so we can overlay kernel timelines against allocation events? current trace file has them but the overlay is noisy. I can run a script to correlate timestamps.

ashley: saved perfetto to https://perf.redwood/2034567890/trace.perfetto and nvprof summary to https://perf.redwood/2034567890/nvprof.txt

perf-bot: checklist updated in thread: [capture stacks, run arena warmup, ramp test 1h, kernel-selector experiment, collect perfetto overlay] (owners: ashley, vikram, marco).

sophia: one more thought — quantization path uses slightly different allocator alignment and caused similar thrash in past. confirm quantized model run too.

vikram: agreed. add quantized run to matrix. also add `MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=0` style knobs for host-side free behavior.

ashley: ack, starting jobs. posting progress here. :thumbsup:

marco: if overnight run looks good, we should codify arena warmup and slab change as safe defaults for models with avg-seq > 256. small risk but huge win for p95 in practice.

ashley: noted. will include perf numbers and a short RFC draft in #eng-runtime tomorrow.

vikram: nice work catching the allocator-kernel coupling. small, pragmatic fixes first, then revisit kernel selector heuristics. :rocket:

sophia: thanks everyone. keep the traces coming.

ashley: final note — temp mitigation: enabling `--allocator-compat=prealloc` reduced eviction storms; pushing patch to gate. will update when merged. :white_check_mark:
